author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page below the first as the first page
summary: Asking the owner listing for a page below the first shows the first page of matches instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given owners matching a search, when the listing is asked for the page before the first, then the first page of matches is listed
given owners matching a search, when the listing is asked for a page several below the first, then the first page is listed and the error page is not shown
non_goals: the veterinarian directory listing, which the owner did not report on
a page beyond the last page of matches
a page value that is not a number
notes: Owner-stated requirement, not derived: quoted request in intake-decision at line 1. The owner recorded no further decisions, so scope is exactly the reported behavior for the owner listing. Boundary check: REQ-OWN-002 states matches are listed a page at a time and says nothing about a page below the first, so no existing requirement is revised and no Non-Goals row is touched. Cause and mechanism are the design stage's call.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Durable memory already places this work. system-design.md Contracts lists OwnerController as owning the server-rendered owner search with paging, and Package Structure keeps controllers, repositories, and entities together in the owner feature package. The fix is a normalization of the requested page inside that controller's existing pagination helper, with no new type, package, dependency, or interface. security-principles.md Trust Boundaries places the check correctly: the page request parameter is external input, the product contract admits a value below the first page, so the boundary normalizes it to the first page rather than rejecting it. Internal code past the boundary keeps its contract, which matters because Spring Data's page index is zero-based and non-negative. Placing the rule in the controller does not deepen Open Question 2 (business rules in controllers): this is request-parameter normalization at the web boundary, not a domain rule about owners. Basis for the coverage claim: full read of OwnerController.java and OwnerControllerTests.java plus a grep over templates; the IDE oracle is not connected, so this is the weaker resolution basis.
integration_points: OwnerController.processFindForm feeds the page value to two consumers: the repository query via the pagination helper, and the currentPage model attribute read by owners/ownersList.html
owners/ownersList.html drives its first, previous, next, and numbered links from currentPage compared against totalPages

patterns.description: existing controller-local pagination helper converting a one-based page parameter into a zero-based PageRequest; the normalization belongs on this path

risks.risk: Normalizing only the repository query leaves currentPage carrying the raw value, so the rendered pagination links echo the un-normalized page back out and the first page is not marked current.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once, before both consumers, and pass the single normalized value to the query and to the model.

risks.risk: VetController carries a structurally identical pagination helper with the same latent behavior, inviting a drive-by fix outside the slice.
risks.mitigation: The veterinarian directory is a recorded slice non-goal. Leave VetController untouched; the two listings declaring their paging independently is already recorded in system-design.md Constants.

risks.risk: Broadening the change into a general page-parameter guard would pull in the two other non-goals, a page beyond the last page and a non-numeric page.
risks.mitigation: Implement exactly the two acceptance criteria. Neither non-goal shares the code path being changed.

notes: No durable-memory edit accompanies this verdict. Known Defects records confirmed defects that remain in the code; this one is fixed by the slice, so no row is added or removed. No ubiquitous-language term is introduced: page and listing are presentation concepts, not domain concepts. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Clamping logic is a single well-named constant (FIRST_PAGE) and Math.max clamp, no magic numbers
The single requestedPage local avoids recomputing the clamp and keeps query and pagination-model values consistent, per its explanatory comment
checkFormat and compileJava both pass clean; no formatting or compilation issues
Change is minimal and scoped to the one method that needed it, no unrelated churn

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Upper-bound behavior is unchanged and left as-is: a very large page (e.g. page=2147483647) yields an empty result and falls into the notFound branch rather than an error, so it is not a defect, but a symmetric clamp against totalPages would make the intent of FIRST_PAGE read as a full range guard.

Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle and this reviewer has no network access. The change set touches no build file, so nothing is introduced, but a human or CI should close the framework-CVE check for Spring Boot 4.1.0 separately.
approved_aspects: Clamping with Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) removes the prior unvalidated-input path where page=0 reached PageRequest.of(-1,...) and surfaced an IllegalArgumentException on the error page, which renders the underlying exception message; the change narrows that disclosure path rather than widening it
Integer.MIN_VALUE no longer reaches the page-1 arithmetic, so the signed-overflow edge on the request-derived page parameter is closed at the boundary

Data access still goes through the derived repository query findByLastNameStartingWith with a PageRequest; no request-derived text enters query text, and page size stays a fixed constant of 5 so the clamp introduces no unbounded allocation

Request-derived values reaching the model (currentPage) are ints rendered through Thymeleaf default escaping; no template preprocessing, no markup injection, no new endpoint, no new binder or identifier binding

No new dependency, credential, secret-shaped literal, logging statement, file or process operation, or deserialization surface appears in the diff; the change set is one controller, its test, and the PRD

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: Three files in one module, eight hunks, no sensitive paths and no binary files; the production edit is confined to OwnerController.processFindForm and the structurally identical VetController pagination helper was deliberately left alone as a recorded non-goal.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks, Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is a pure lower clamp: for any page of one or more the value is unchanged, so no existing paging behavior moves, and the single requestedPage local reaches both consumers, the PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5) query and the currentPage model attribute the pagination template renders, so the query and the links cannot disagree.

test_adequacy.note: The two new MockMvc tests exercise the real binding and dispatch path at page=0 and page=-7, and they would fail against the unfixed code because PageRequest.of(-1, 5) throws before the stubbed repository is ever reached; the currentPage is 1 assertion covers the model consumer rather than only the status, so neither test is tautological.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved in a single round with empty findings and zero build retries; the two recommendations are not reservations about this diff, since the test-reviewer's parameterized-test suggestion is labelled non-blocking and future-facing, and the security-reviewer's symmetric-upper-clamp note names a recorded slice non-goal while its unverified-NVD note is a standing project gap invariant to a change that touches no build file.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations and zero build retries; the changed paths and the two test method names match the prd-entry's file_targets and test_names exactly, and the three declared non-goals, the vet directory, a page beyond the last, and a non-numeric page, are all untouched.

rationale: The clamp is a pure lower bound applied once before both the query and the pagination model, so no page of one or more changes behavior, and the tests fail against the unfixed code. Confirm and merge; the unverified Spring Boot CVE check is a standing project gap, not this change.
